title: Sweet Potato & Spicy Sausage Quesadillas

overview.description: Crisp flour tortillas filled with roasted sweet potato, spicy sausage, melted cheese and onion.

ingredients: 600g sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes
250g spicy sausage, removed from its casing and crumbled
method: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Toss the sweet potato with half the olive oil, the smoked paprika, cumin, chilli powder if using, salt and black pepper.
Spread the sweet potato on a baking tray.
Roast for 25–30 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly caramelised.
While the sweet potato cooks, heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan.
Add the spicy sausage and cook until browned and cooked through.
Add the red onion and red pepper.
Cook until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Remove from the heat.
Add the roasted sweet potato to the sausage mixture and gently combine.
Heat a large dry frying pan over medium heat.
Place one tortilla in the pan.
Spread cheese over half of the tortilla.
Add some of the sweet potato and sausage filling.
Add a little more cheese.
Fold the tortilla over the filling.
Cook until the underside is golden and crisp.
Carefully turn the quesadilla and cook until the other side is golden and the cheese has melted.
Repeat with the remaining tortillas and filling.
Cut into wedges and serve.

learning.did-you-know: Quesadillas get their name from queso, the Spanish word for cheese. The cheese melts between tortillas or inside folded tortillas, while the other fillings can vary enormously.
learning.what-you-will-learn: How roasting concentrates the sweetness of vegetables and how cheese helps bind fillings together inside a crisp tortilla.

notes.why-its-in-the-chapman-kitchen: A family-friendly meal that combines sweet potato with spicy sausage and melted cheese in a format that is easy to customise and works well for batch preparation.
chapman-tips: Cut the sweet potato into small cubes so it cooks quickly and develops plenty of caramelised edges.
Roasting the sweet potato gives it much more flavour than boiling.
Don't overfill the quesadillas or they will be difficult to turn.
Use enough cheese to help hold the filling together.
A moderately hot pan gives the tortilla time to crisp while the cheese melts.
The heat level can be adjusted by changing the sausage or adding chilli separately.
A little lime juice or fresh coriander works particularly well with the sweet potato.
notes.batch-cooking: Good for batch cooking. Prepare the filling in advance and refrigerate it until needed. Assembled quesadillas can be cooked and frozen, although freshly cooked quesadillas have the best texture.
notes.leftovers: Leftover filling can be used in omelettes, wraps, sandwiches or on top of baked potatoes.
